summary: Belgium is part of the Schengen Area: EU citizens travel freely, and Swiss and EEA nationals enter with a valid identity card or passport; nationals of the countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806) can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period (ETIAS is not yet in operation), and nationals on the EU's visa-required list (Annex I) need a Schengen short-stay visa (€90 under the Visa Code, €35 for Armenian, Azerbaijani and Belarusian nationals under EU visa facilitation agreements, and 75% of the standard fee for Cabo Verdean nationals). Belgium's embassy pages say the application is submitted at the Belgian embassy when Belgium is the first entry into the Schengen zone and/or the main purpose of the trip lies in Belgium.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Belgium?
faq.answer: EU citizens travel freely with a valid passport or ID card, and Swiss and EEA nationals enter with a valid identity card or passport. Citizens of the countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806) can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period without a visa. Nationals on the EU's visa-required list (Annex I) need a Schengen short-stay visa (€90 under the Visa Code, €35 for Armenian, Azerbaijani and Belarusian nationals under EU visa facilitation agreements, and 75% of the standard fee for Cabo Verdean nationals), submitted at the Belgian embassy when Belgium is the first entry into the Schengen zone and/or the main purpose of the trip.

faq.question: How much does a Belgium Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: €90 for adults, €45 for children aged six to under 12, and waived for children under six, under the EU Visa Code. Under EU visa facilitation agreements Armenian, Azerbaijani and Belarusian nationals pay €35, and Cabo Verdean nationals 75% of the standard fee.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Belgium?
faq.answer: ETIAS is the new EU travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers to enter 30 European countries. It is currently not in operation and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. The official ETIAS website lists a EUR 20 application fee.

faq.question: How do I stay in Belgium longer than 90 days?
faq.answer: Belgium's embassy pages say a national long-stay (type D) visa is for a stay in Belgium of more than 90 days, for academic purposes (student and student exchange), economic purposes (single permit, au pair, professional card), family reunification, marriage or legal cohabitation with intention of permanent stay, and retirement.

faq.question: Can EU citizens enter Belgium with just an ID card?
faq.answer: Yes for EU citizens: Your Europe says they can travel freely carrying either a valid passport or a national identity card, and EU law says no entry visa may be imposed on them. The EU–Swiss free movement agreement lets Swiss nationals enter simply upon production of a valid identity card or passport, and the EEA Agreement incorporates the EU free movement directive for EEA nationals.
